Don't travel by air, says Supreme Court; refuses urgent listing of plea alleging 700% hike in airfares
 Centre says aviation rules under Bharatiya Vayuyan Adhiniyam being fast-tracked to curb volatility and ensure passenger protection
 Updated - November 02, 2026 04:46 pm IST - New Delhi 
 PTI READ LATER 
 SEE ALL 
 Remove 
 The Supreme Court tells the petitioner to avoid air travel and refuses urgent listing despite a more than 700% spike in airfare. File (Representational image)
 | Photo Credit: PTI
 Don’t travel by air, the Supreme Court told a petitioner on Monday (November 2, 2026) while refusing urgent listing of a plea alleging nearly 700% increase in airfares.
 New rules to regulate volatile airfares to be published in two weeks, Centre tells SC An advocate mentioned the matter for urgent listing before a Bench comprising Justices Vikram Nath, Sandeep Mehta and Aparesh Kumar Singh.
 “The aviation fare has increased by 700%,” the advocate said.
 “Don’t travel by air,” the Bench observed.
 The advocate then said air travel is an essential service. “It’s a violation of Article 14.”
 Article 14 of the Constitution deals with equality before law.
 Airfares need to be ‘rationalised’, says Supreme Court The Supreme Court is already hearing a separate petition filed by social activist S. Laxminarayanan, who has sought a robust and independent regulator that ensures transparency and passenger protection across the civil aviation sector and regulatory guidelines to control “unpredictable fluctuations” in airfare and ancillary charges imposed by private airlines in India.
 During a hearing on that plea on October 16, the Centre informed the Supreme Court that administrative approval has been granted to rules under a 2024 legislation aimed at regulating India’s aviation sector, and is likely to be published in two weeks.
 SC asks Centre to place on record new aviation rules to regulate volatile airfares The Supreme Court had asked Solicitor General Tushar Mehta to place the published rules under the Bharatiya Vayuyan Adhiniyam, 2024, before the court on the next date of hearing — November 16.
 On August 17, the Centre told the Supreme Court that it had fast-tracked the framing of rules under the Bharatiya Vayuyan Adhiniyam, aimed at modernising India’s aviation sector.
 In November last year, the Supreme Court sought responses from the Centre and others on Mr. Laxminarayanan’s plea.
 Airfare surges during festivals ‘exploitative’, says Supreme Court While hearing the matter in January, the Supreme Court had said it would interfere with the “unpredictable fluctuations” in airfares and flagged the exorbitant rise during festivals.
 It had termed the exorbitant hike of fares by airlines “exploitation” and asked the Centre and the Directorate General of Civil Aviation to file their replies on the plea.
